rows.text: March 9, 2006
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.00%) for the intermeeting period.
In the real economy, exports continue to exhibit steady growth, the recovery of private consumption has been maintained, and facilities investment is still recovering gradually.
The Bank of Korea
Monetary Policy Decision
On the other hand, an improvement of construction investment has not yet been sufficient.
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.00%) for the intermeeting period.
Meanwhile, the current account is still running a surplus, although its scale has narrowed in reflection of the increased import demand.
Both consumer price inflation and core inflation maintain overall stability.
(The following is an unofficial English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
In the real economy, exports continue to exhibit steady growth, the recovery of private consumption has been maintained, and facilities investment is still recovering gradually.
Nevertheless, there are latent inflationary pressures due to the economic recovery and persistently high oil prices.
The recent rebound in real estate prices has continued centering on certain areas.
On the other hand, an improvement of construction investment has not yet been sufficient.
Meanwhile, the current account is still running a surplus, although its scale has narrowed in reflection of the increased import demand.
In the financial markets, overall liquidity conditions are favorable and financial institutions‘ loans continue to increase steadily led by those to small and medium enterprises.
Both consumer price inflation and core inflation maintain overall stability.

Taking the above economic and financial conditions into consideration, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.00%) for the intermeeting period.
Nevertheless, there are latent inflationary pressures due to the economic recovery and persistently high oil prices.
The recent rebound in real estate prices has continued centering on certain areas.
In the financial markets, overall liquidity conditions are favorable and financial institutions' loans continue to increase steadily led by those to small and medium enterprises.

Taking the above economic and financial conditions into consideration, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.00%) for the intermeeting period.
